# amdgpu (Phoenix1, gfx1103): unrecoverable GPU page fault from Brave (Chromium) GPU process kills GNOME Shell session

## Summary

On a Framework Laptop 13 (AMD Ryzen 5 7640U / Radeon 760M, Phoenix1 iGPU, PCI ID `1002:15bf`), the Brave browser's GPU process intermittently triggers a `[gfxhub] page fault` from the graphics ring (`ring 24`, compute/SQC client). The driver's per-ring reset path fails (`Ring gfx_0.0.0 reset failed`) and falls back to a full MODE2 GPU reset. The reset succeeds at the hardware level (`GPU reset succeeded`, `device wedged, but recovered through reset`), but the GNOME Shell (Mutter) Wayland compositor's GL context is destroyed in the process and GNOME Shell aborts with `SIGABRT (signal 6)`, terminating the user session.

**User-visible impact**: the screen briefly goes black and the user is dropped back to the GDM login screen, losing all unsaved state in every running application.

The bug reproduces across kernel updates and across two completely different Brave installation methods (Snap and official `.deb`), so it is not caused by AppArmor sandboxing or distro packaging. It appears to be a real interaction between Chromium's GPU process workload and the Phoenix1 amdgpu driver, where the failed per-ring reset is the proximate cause of user-visible session loss.

issues.title: Wayland mouse movement causes CPU computation errors under heavy load with AMD Graphics Stack 31.30
issues.author: Takuro Ashie
issues.description:
## Environment

* CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT
* Chipset: AMD X570
* GPU: Radeon RX 9070 XT
* Ubuntu 24.04 and Ubuntu 26.04
* AMD Graphics Stack 31.30 (installed via `amdgpu-install` with the default options)
* GNOME Wayland
* KDE Plasma Wayland

## Summary

After installing AMD Graphics Stack 31.30, CPU-intensive workloads become unstable under Wayland.

While a heavy CPU workload is running (Prime95, Chromium build, Linux kernel build, DKMS build, etc.), simply moving the mouse continuously causes failures within a few seconds.

The same hardware is completely stable when using the Ubuntu default open-source graphics stack.

## Symptoms

The issue is reproducible with multiple workloads.

Prime95 (`mprime`) fails with:

```text
FATAL ERROR: Rounding was 0.5, expected less than 0.4
Hardware failure detected
```

Chromium, Linux kernel, and DKMS builds also fail with random compiler crashes such as:

* GCC Internal Compiler Error (Segmentation fault in cc1)
* Clang/LLVM crashes
* Random build failures at different source files

The failure location varies between runs.

## Reproduction

### 1. Install AMD Graphics Stack

Install AMD Graphics Stack 31.30 using the default installation:

```bash
sudo amdgpu-install

issues.title: amdgpu: deferred drm .release clears pci drvdata owned by another driver (vfio-pci), NULL-deref on unbind/runtime-PM
issues.author: Faruk Aydin
issues.description:
## Summary

`amdgpu_driver_release_kms()` calls `pci_set_drvdata(adev->pdev, NULL)` (drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_kms.c:1608 in v7.1.2). This function is the DRM `.release` callback, so it runs at the _final_ `drm_dev_put()` — which is deferred until the last userspace reference to the DRM device is dropped, not at unbind time.

In a GPU-passthrough workflow (unbind amdgpu -\> bind vfio-pci, standard VFIO practice), any process still holding the dGPU's DRM node open at unbind time (a GPU monitoring daemon such as LACT, a compositor, etc.) delays the final release past the point where vfio-pci has bound the device and stored its own drvdata. When the last DRM fd closes, amdgpu's deferred release then NULLs **vfio-pci's** drvdata.

Every subsequent vfio-pci path that dereferences drvdata crashes:

- `vfio_pci_remove` -\> `vfio_pci_core_unregister_device` -\> `vfio_pci_core_sriov_configure` (on unbind) — observed, oops attached

issues.title: amdgpu: BUG_ON in amdgpu_device_mm_access on re-probe of Navi 48 after VFIO passthrough
issues.author: Faruk Aydin
issues.description:
## Summary

Re-probing a Navi 48 (RX 9070 XT, 1002:7550) with amdgpu after the card has been used by a VM via vfio-pci hits:

```
kernel BUG at drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_device.c:720!
```

which is

```c
BUG_ON(!IS_ALIGNED(pos, 4) || !IS_ALIGNED(size, 4));
```

in `amdgpu_device_mm_access()`, called from `amdgpu_discovery_init()` while reading the IP-discovery table out of VRAM. After a VM has run on the card, the discovery TMR location/size the driver computes from device state is garbage (unaligned), and the driver BUG()s instead of failing probe.

This worked on v7.0.12 (same card, same reclaim flow, dozens of cycles) and regressed by v7.1.2.

## Impact goes beyond the crash

The BUG kills the probing task mid-`really_probe()`. Since the driver core sets `dev->driver` and creates the sysfs driver link _before_ calling probe, the device is left as a zombie: `lspci -k` / sysfs claim "Kernel driver in use: amdgpu", but no DRM device exists (no `drm/` sysfs dir, no /dev/dri node) and probe's error path never ran. Any later interaction with

this half-bound device (including a subsequent unbind) operates on inconsistent state. Only a reboot recovers the GPU for host use.

Requested behavior: validate the discovery blob location/size read from the device and fail probe with an error (as other discovery-validation paths already do) instead of BUG_ON on device-provided data.

issues.author: Bob
issues.description:
## Summary

On an AMD Radeon 680M (Rembrandt, gfx10.3, RDNA2 APU) the graphics ring intermittently takes a GPUVM permission page fault from the TCP (texture cache) UTCL2 client while the desktop X server (Xorg with Glamor on radeonsi GL) is doing heavy texture upload and compositing. The fault is a permission fault on a page that is already mapped (`MAPPING_ERROR=0`, `WALKER_ERROR=0`, `PERMISSION_FAULTS=0x3`, read access). ## Brief summary of the problem:

When the RX 9070 XT (eGPU connected via OCuLink) is in a deep idle state — SCLK at 4–60 MHz, GPU Load at 0–1% — ring submissions from kwin_wayland (GFX flip), DXVK (SDMA + GFX), or VKD3D (compute) time out after 60 seconds. The GPU does not wake from GFXOFF before the ring watchdog fires.

issues.title: GPU reset over Thunderbolt causes hard system lock (RDNA 4 / GFX12, Navi 48)
issues.author: Keith Wood
issues.description:
## Summary

When an RDNA 4 GPU (RX 9060 XT, `1002:7590`) is connected via a Thunderbolt eGPU dock, any GPU reset attempt (triggered by GFX ring timeout under 3D load) causes a hard system lock requiring power cycle. The PCIe hot-reset does not propagate correctly through the Thunderbolt bridge chain, leaving the PCIe link in a bad state where any subsequent MMIO access hangs the CPU.

**Workaround:** `amdgpu.gpu_recovery=0` — disabling GPU reset prevents the *hard lock* (the CPU hang that follows a failed reset). The system survives the failure in a recoverable state (clean reboot) instead of locking hard. Note: this does **not** prevent the underlying crashes — the GPU still dies under sustained 3D load, it just fails survivably. See later comments for details. _(Edited 2026-06-18 to correct an earlier overstatement that gaming "works perfectly" with this parameter.)_

## Bug Description

On RDNA4 (Navi 48, RX 9070 XT), the `/sys/class/drm/cardN/device/pp_dpm_mclk` sysfs file does **not** mark the currently active memory clock state with `*` during active 3D rendering. This behaviour differs from RDNA2 (RX 6800 XT), where the active state is always marked.

## pp_dpm_mclk content at idle (correct)

```
0: 96Mhz *
1: 456Mhz 
2: 772Mhz 
3: 875Mhz 
4: 1124Mhz 
5: 1258Mhz 
```

## pp_dpm_mclk content during active 3D load (bug)

```
0: 96Mhz 
1: 456Mhz 
2: 772Mhz 
3: 875Mhz 
4: 1124Mhz 
5: 1258Mhz 
```

No `*` marker on any line during the entire duration of a 3D workload (tested with FurMark). The marker reappears a few seconds after the workload ends.

## hwmon behaviour (correct)

The hwmon interface correctly reflects the actual memory clock at all times:
```
/sys/class/hwmon/hwmonN/freq2_input  # label: mclk
```

issues.title: amdgpu (RX 590): GTT memory leak on resume from suspend (partially improved in 6.17 but not fixed)
issues.author: Ricardo Sanz
issues.description:
**Human briefing**

It seems there is a memory leak on resume from suspend, with `/sys/class/drm/card1/device/mem_info_gtt_used` bumping several hundreds megabytes.

`cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/1/amdgpu_evict_gtt` makes the system reduce the mem_info_gtt_used value to around 70MB.

I've tested it with IA help. Kernel 6.17 improved the situation but still happens (just less memory leaked). 

**IA report (reviewed by a human)**

---

---

#### Description

On resume from suspend (S3), the amdgpu driver leaks GTT memory (system RAM pinned for GPU access) that is not released back to the OS. The leak accumulates across sleep/wake cycles and persists until reboot. The kernel must compensate by dropping page cache to keep the system running.

Additionally, each resume cycle permanently fragments the kernel's direct map: 2M page mappings are split into 4K pages (due to write-combined GTT pages), and these splits are never consolidated until reboot.

#### Measurements

**Kernel 6.8.0-117:**

|  | Value |
|--|-------|
| GTT before sleep | 687 MB |
| GTT after wake | 1,823 MB |
| **Leaked per cycle** | **+1,136 MB** |
| DirectMap4k increase per cycle | +260 MB (2M → 4K splits) |

**Kernel 6.17.0-29:**

|  | Value |
|--|-------|
| GTT before sleep | 213 MB |
| GTT after wake | 904 MB |
| **Leaked per cycle** | **+691 MB** |
| DirectMap4k increase per cycle | +260 MB (2M → 4K splits) |

Progress between 6.8 → 6.17: baseline GTT reduced by 474 MB, leak per cycle reduced by 445 MB (\~39%).

**1. Issue:**\
When locking the screen (Meta+L) on KDE Plasma Wayland, the screen momentarily outputs a vertically split green and black frame for 1-2 seconds before the actual lock screen appears.

issues.title: `amdgpu: [CRTC:416:crtc-0] hw_done or flip_done timed out` -- RX 9070 (Navi 48 / DCN 4.0.1) freezes KWin Wayland after GPU MODE1 reset
issues.author: Dobbelklick
issues.description:
## Description

### What happens

The primary monitor freezes completely under KWin Wayland. The GPU undergoes an autonomous **MODE1 reset** at runtime; after the reset the display subsystem appears to be left in a broken state (wrong GL texture dimensions observed immediately after reset). Roughly 11 minutes later the first `flip_done timed out` error occurs, followed by an endless loop of pageflip timeouts that freeze the compositor permanently. The system itself remains alive.

Additionally, `REG_WAIT timeout 1us * 150000 tries - optc401_disable_crtc line:235` appears on **every single boot** during DCN initialization, even when no freeze follows -- suggesting a pre-existing issue with the Optical Timing Controller on DCN 4.0.1.

### Timeline (from journal, 2025-05-22)

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| 14:58:14 | Boot -- `REG_WAIT timeout optc401_disable_crtc:235` (twice, every boot) |
| 21:15:24 | **GPU MODE1 reset** (`amdgpu: GPU smu mode1 reset`) |
| 21:15:27 | KWin: `GL_INVALID_VALUE in glTexSubImage2D(xoffset 0 + width 2466 > 1920)` -- compositor confused about resolution post-reset |
| 21:26:56 | Kernel: `[CRTC:416:crtc-0] flip_done timed out` -- first timeout |
| 21:26:59 | Kernel: `[CRTC:416:crtc-0] hw_done or flip_done timed out` -- compositor frozen |
| 21:33:39 | Kernel: `[CRTC:416:crtc-0] commit wait timed out`, `[PLANE:413:plane-7] commit wait timed out` |
| 21:34:00 | Further `flip_done timed out` -- no recovery, reboot required |
